newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber end up sharply to limit on cash ideas.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber end up sharply to limit on cash ideas.

text.p: Nearby CME lumber futures ended up their $10 limit as expectations for firmer cash prices and a bullish construction report boosted prices, traders said.
January finished limit up at $402.20 per tbf, with March limit up at $388.70. Other months rose $6.80 to $8.00.
Carryover demand from Friday reflected anticipation that cash markets would firm on the heels of Thanksgiving.
"They (traders) expect a pick up in retail demand after the holiday," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney forest products analyst.
Cash sources said some mills are increasing asking prices, which could indicate a pickup in demand. Also, a few mills are starting to talk about year end closures.

A bullish construction report fueled strength and pushed prices into buy stops early. U.S. Commerce Department said October construction spending up 1.8 percent, the largest one-month increase since March. Economists had predicted a 1.0 percent decline.
Trading limits will be expanded to $15.00 Tuesday due to limit gains in January the past two trading sessions.
